column1: # THE SHARED REAP CASE TABLE — read by BOTH implementations, with identical expected values.
# PROJECT_PLAN.md's Risks section names shared-helper divergence as the crux of this port:
# borg_reap_overlay and _borg_should_reap stay live in zsh (nine call sites) while Python
# reimplements them, and divergence shows up as `borg link` saying idle while `borg next` says
# waiting — a plausible-looking wrong answer with no crash, the exact failure mode this repo has
# been bitten by three times. The stated mitigation is ONE case table exercised by both sides.
#   tests/reaper_cases.bats          reads it and runs lib/reaper.sh + borg_reap_overlay under zsh
#   borg_core/link/test_core.py      reads it and runs core.should_reap + core.reap_overlay
# Both readers assert the SAME expected column. A row that disagrees fails one side loudly instead
#   id          stable identifier, referenced in failure messages
#   status      the project's status as the registry/state.json holds it; EMPTY means ""
#               (spelled out, never left blank: a blank column is two consecutive tabs, and zsh's
#               `read` with a whitespace IFS collapses them and shifts every later field left --
#               the same trap lib/registry.zsh:213-217 documents for its own @tsv stream)
#   age         last_activity, expressed RELATIVE to the test's "now" so no row rots:
#                 NOW-<seconds>   that many seconds in the past
#                 NOW+<seconds>   that many seconds in the FUTURE
#   live        1 if a live tmux window matches, else 0
#   threshold   BORG_REAP_STALE_HOURS; GARBAGE means a non-integer value
#   why         one line, for the failure message
# Boundary rows use offsets far from an hour boundary on purpose. An earlier draft had a row at
# exactly 3600s against a 1h threshold, which flips on a sub-second timing difference between
# fixture setup and evaluation; every boundary here is probed with >= 60s of slack.

column7: why
idle is not a reapable status
archived is not a reapable status
an unrecognized status is not reapable
an empty status is not reapable
the status match is case-sensitive
a live window is never reaped however stale
same, for waiting
liveness is checked before the missing-timestamp rule
no last_activity at all means reap
the literal string null counts as no timestamp
an unparseable timestamp reaps, unlike relative_time which echoes it
a garbage threshold still reaps a project with no timestamp
a non-integer threshold makes the shell test return 2, read as keep
one hour old, well inside a twelve hour threshold
a day old, well past it
same, for waiting
11h50m: under the threshold by ten minutes
12h10m: over it by ten minutes
a zero threshold reaps anything at or past its timestamp
TRUNCATION: shell arithmetic gives -100/3600 = 0, so 0 >= 0 reaps
-7200/3600 = -2, which is below the threshold
a future timestamp is never stale against a positive threshold
a day old is nowhere near a 999 hour threshold
